resources.string: The app drops these packets before decryption — no CPU, battery or storage is spent, and nothing is shown. But the bytes already reached the radio, and you paid for them. That is how any open network works: whoever knows the address can send.
Drop the connections — data stops being spent at once. Messages will not arrive until you return.
The only way to cut the stream and stay online. Contacts are kept — they receive the new address.
Blocked sources are already cut at the lowest level — their packets go no further than the transport.
Your identity does not change: name, fingerprint, history and groups stay the same. Only the address you are found by changes. Anyone you do not tell will lose contact with you.
Source of the flood — unchecked by default
Will be told when they come online

Both this device and the password are required. A copy taken off the phone is useless without the password.
A forgotten password cannot be recovered — the messages will be lost. That is by design: a way in for you is a way in for anyone.

A copy of your messages, not of your identity. The key (24 words) is stored separately: the key restores who the network sees you as, this copy restores what you read.
Large files do not fit into the archive, but they can be downloaded from the sender again — they are addressed by content.

Group messages are included, keys are not: the archive restores what to read, not what to decrypt with. A restored group state would be stale and would break the group for everyone, so the group opens read-only until you are invited again.
The file will leave the phone — to a cloud, a card, another computer. This device\'s key is not available there, so the archive is locked with a password and opens anywhere.
A forgotten password cannot be recovered: the archive becomes a dead file. That is by design — a way in for you is a way in for anyone who finds the file.
The system will ask where to save the file.
Keep this screen open. Checking the password takes about a second — deliberately: it costs the same to anyone trying to guess it.
